title: Social Security 2026 COLA Increase Explained Simply
bigPicture: COLA stands for Cost-of-Living Adjustment, and it's a yearly bump to your Social Security check meant to help your money keep up with rising prices.
whatYouNeedToKnow: COLA is not a raise — it's a adjustment to offset inflation, so your buying power stays roughly the same.
The exact percentage for 2026 has not been officially announced yet; watch for the SSA's October 2025 update.
Your specific increase depends on the benefit type you receive — retirement, disability, or SSI payments may differ slightly.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming COLA applies equally to everyone — some people with Medicare Part B premiums may see little or no net gain.
Waiting until December to check your new amount — review your my Social Security account as soon as the notice arrives.
actionSteps: Log in to your my Social Security account at ssa.gov to confirm your payment details once the 2026 COLA is announced.
Set a calendar reminder for October 2025 so you don't miss the official COLA announcement.
